title: Kids With the Greatest Number of Candies
statement:
Kid `i` holds `candies[i]` candies, and you have `extraCandies` more to hand out. For each kid separately, imagine giving that one kid all of the `extraCandies` while everyone else keeps their own amount.

Return a list of booleans of the same length as `candies` whose entry `i` is `true` exactly when kid `i` would then have at least as many candies as every other kid (sharing the top amount with others still counts), and `false` otherwise.
notes:
## Intuition

Giving every candy to one kid only raises that kid's total; the others stay put. So the kid ends up on top exactly when the new total reaches the largest amount anyone already has. Comparing each kid with every other kid works in O(n²), but one pass to find that largest amount lets each kid be judged with a single comparison.

## Approach

1. Scan `candies` once to find `most`, the largest amount any kid holds.
2. For each `count` in `candies`, push whether `count + extraCandies >= most` into `result`.
3. Return `result`.

## Example 1, step by step

`candies = [2, 3, 5, 1, 3]`, `extraCandies = 3`, so `most = 5`. The new totals are `5, 6, 8, 4, 6`. Only `4` falls short of `5`, giving `[true, true, true, false, true]`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): one pass for the maximum and one for the answers.
- Space: O(1) besides the returned list.

## Pitfalls

- Use `>=`, not `>`: tying with the current leader still counts as having the most.
- Compare with the original maximum; the extra candies go to one kid at a time, never to the leader as well.
- Find the maximum before building the answers, not while doing so.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `most` | the largest number of candies any kid has before the gift |
| `count` | one kid's own number of candies |
| `result` | the list of answers, one per kid |

narration.2: Start the running maximum below every possible amount.
narration.3: Look at every kid's amount once.
narration.4: Keep the largest amount seen so far.
narration.6: The answers go here, one per kid, in order.
narration.7: Now judge each kid in turn.
narration.8: With all the extra candies this kid is on top exactly when the total reaches the maximum.
narration.10: Return one true or false per kid.
